WEBVTT

NOTE Generated from docs/tour/out/beats.json; timings are the recorded video clock.

00:00:05.395 --> 00:00:10.440
This run maps one configured source root: website slash K B.

00:00:10.440 --> 00:00:15.486
Its 254 notes and 554 edges come from that knowledge base, not the whole workspace.

00:00:15.486 --> 00:00:20.531
Synapse can ingest one root or several.

00:00:20.531 --> 00:00:27.629
Open the glossary and the graph starts speaking.

00:00:27.629 --> 00:00:34.727
Hue alone would only tell you which repository a note came from — useless once a brain is one repo.

00:00:34.727 --> 00:00:41.825
So a node class says what a note IS: articles are gold stars, each social channel keeps its own colour, and media splits by kind.

00:00:41.825 --> 00:00:48.923
21 classes, matched on each note's own path and name.

00:00:48.923 --> 00:00:54.342
These counts are live.

00:00:54.342 --> 00:00:59.762
Whatever this brain currently holds is what the legend reports — hero images, carousel slides, LinkedIn cards, videos, interactive bundles.

00:00:59.762 --> 00:01:05.181
The tour reads the same live legend the application uses.

00:01:05.181 --> 00:01:10.425
Close it, and the shapes stay legible on their own.

00:01:10.425 --> 00:01:18.292
Type, and matches light up across the whole graph at once.

00:01:18.292 --> 00:01:26.159
Press Enter and the top hit opens — the camera flies to it, and the note renders as a wiki article on the right.

00:01:26.159 --> 00:01:32.492
This is an article root.

00:01:32.492 --> 00:01:38.826
Hover any node and the graph tells you what it is, where it came from, and how connected it is.

00:01:38.826 --> 00:01:45.159
Around it sit the things that belong to it.

00:01:45.159 --> 00:01:52.454
Scroll to zoom.

00:01:52.454 --> 00:01:59.750
On a big brain the canvas shows the most-connected window first and reveals the long tail as you go in — so the map stays readable as the selected knowledge grows.

00:01:59.751 --> 00:02:09.422
The squares are social posts, and the colour is the channel — LinkedIn blue, X grey, Reddit orange.

00:02:09.422 --> 00:02:19.094
Each one is its own file, linked back to the article it came from.

00:02:19.094 --> 00:02:28.765
You can see at a glance which articles have channel-specific post records.

00:02:28.766 --> 00:02:38.561
Media is first class.

00:02:38.561 --> 00:02:48.355
A hero image, a carousel, an interactive bundle — each is a real node with a real edge, because the reference was resolved at ingest, not guessed at render time.

00:02:48.355 --> 00:02:58.150
What you see and what the graph links are the same file.

00:02:58.150 --> 00:03:07.052
Drag empty space to pan the map.

00:03:07.052 --> 00:03:15.953
Drag a node instead and it stays where you put it — the layout is yours to arrange, and it survives while you work.

00:03:15.953 --> 00:03:33.157
On the right, the same note is a readable article: wikilinks are clickable, and the media the graph linked renders inline — the hero at the top, the interactive figure in place, sized by the figure itself.

00:03:33.158 --> 00:03:42.457
That figure is a live bundle from the repository, running inside a sandbox with no route back to the app or the API.

00:03:42.457 --> 00:03:51.756
Untrusted input, rendered safely — you can read the piece exactly as it ships.

00:03:51.756 --> 00:04:00.038
At the foot of every note is its connections — grouped by how the link was made: a wikilink, a relative path, a sibling in the same folder, an asset.

00:04:00.038 --> 00:04:08.320
Click one and you are reading the neighbour.

00:04:08.320 --> 00:04:20.918
Path mode answers a different question: not "what is near this", but "how do these two things relate at all".

00:04:20.918 --> 00:04:33.516
Pick two notes and the shortest chain of real links between them glows, hop by hop.

00:04:33.516 --> 00:04:41.514
A link pointing at nothing is not hidden.

00:04:41.514 --> 00:04:49.513
Ghosts draws every unresolved reference as a hollow node beside whatever referred to it, and says which kind it is: a note not written yet, a file the brain never ingested, or a dead path.

00:04:49.513 --> 00:04:57.511
The brain admits its own gaps.

00:04:57.511 --> 00:05:04.012
Everything here is derived.

00:05:04.012 --> 00:05:10.512
The notes are plain markdown on your disk; the graph is rebuilt from them and can be thrown away at any time.

00:05:10.512 --> 00:05:17.013
Point Synapse at one repository root or several, and it builds the same kind of map from the knowledge you choose.
